note: A slow, quiet slide over the two octaves of the staff, from the lowest Do to the highest, over a drone in C, the key that gives a tenor two whole octaves, so the key is the lesson and there are no moves. The why says what the slide does to the break, the feel to reach is a line with no jump, and the one care line keeps the top light.

exercise.title: A slide over two octaves
exercise.why: A slide over two octaves passes the spot where your voice wants to break, and going through it slowly and quietly is what smooths it out.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Slide from the lowest {{1}} on the staff up to the highest and back down, slowly and quietly. Sing it on "oo".
Where your line jumps, slide through that spot again, slower and quieter.
Practice until your line runs from the bottom to the top with no jump in it.
_Don't reach for high notes by pushing: let the top of the slide go light._
